methods: Independent combinatorial hypergeometric probability-ordering Fisher calculation for every enumeration state
Independent closed-form 2x2 Pearson and Yates statistics and chi-square tail probabilities
Binomial probability masses sum to one for every null and alternative scenario
Every pointwise Type-I error and power matches independent weighted rejection sums using p < 0.05
Seeded Monte Carlo counts match lookup results for all scenarios without rerunning the production script
Independent Wilson interval and MCSE algebra matches all CSV rows
Conditional fixed-margin Fisher probability mass and rejection event match
Paired exact p-value from 2*sum(Binomial(30,0.5) probabilities for 0:5) and continuity-corrected McNemar statistic match
Crude prevalence ratio, cross-product odds ratio, their SRS confidence intervals and baseline curve identities match

reporting_notes: Caption test_size_curve.png explicitly: lines/points are exact enumeration; error bars are 95% Wilson intervals around Monte Carlo rejection rates. Exact enumeration itself has no Monte Carlo uncertainty.

warnings_seen is initialized but no handler populates it. An empty result.json warnings array is therefore not evidence of a warning-free execution. Keep this limitation or use the actual process log; the independent audit process emitted startup LC_* locale warnings, then passed after the script set its UTF-8 locale.
result.json rounds conditional_fisher_typeI to 0.023 because of JSON serialization defaults; the CSV supports the more precise value 0.02301413756522116. Treat the CSV as the numerical authority.
OR_relative_overstatement_pct is a numerical discrepancy if OR is interpreted as PR, not an error in the OR estimand.
The baseline CSV omits infeasible PR*p0>=1 grid points rather than retaining NA rows. All exported points satisfy the feasible prevalence domain.
All inference in these expansions is SRS educational inference or synthetic paired inference. It does not validate the NHANES complex-sampling inference.
